title: SSO & Admin Event Sensitivity Tiering for RBAC v2 Audit Pipeline
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Introduce sensitivity-based tiering for SSO/SAML and admin-related audit events as part of RBAC v2. Goals: ensure high-fidelity retention for high-sensitivity events (e.g., role changes, grant escalations, SSO assertion failures), reduce storage costs for low-value telemetry, and provide per-tenant cost guardrails and fast query paths for security investigations.
background: RBAC v2 expands administrative surfaces and increases volume of identity and admin events. Current audit pipeline stores everything uniformly which inflates hot-storage costs and slows forensic queries. Compliance teams require 1yr WORM for sensitive admin changes while product telemetry can use shorter retention. This ticket designs ingestion-side classification, dynamic partitioning and retention rules, and cost-aware backpressure so we meet SLAs without unbounded storage growth.
proposed_solution: Event sensitivity classification at ingest: enrich SSO/SAML and admin events with sensitivity tag (high|medium|low) using deterministic ruleset + allowlist of sensitive event types (role.create, role.update, role.bind, scoped-grant, sso-failures, admin-console-access).

Two-path ingestion: high-sensitivity -> low-latency hot index + write-once cold object store copy (S3 WORM); medium -> hot index with shorter TTL and optional snapshot to cold store; low -> compacted metrics stream (rollups) stored in warm tier only.

Tenant-aware partitioning: partition hot index by tenant_id + sensitivity to enable tenant-scoped retention and efficient purge/eviction. Use time-based rolling segments with sensitivity-aware shard sizing.

Per-tenant cost guardrails: estimate storage impact at ingest using event weight model; when tenant exceeds configurable budget, automatically apply sampling to low-sensitivity events and emit billing/alerting signals and throttling hints.
Query-time helpers: precompute sensitivity-aware summaries and maintain a fast-access audit-lookup index for high-sensitivity events to accelerate investigations.
Ingest backpressure: integrate with routing layer to apply per-tenant token-bucket limits and drop or sample low-sensitivity events when downstream write latency crosses SLO thresholds.
Retention automation: retention policies driven by sensitivity label with API for compliance exports and on-demand WORM snapshot requests for specific tenants/events.
Operational UX: Console controls for security admins to tune sensitivity rules, view storage forecast, and request ad-hoc retention extensions for investigations.

Implementation path: prototype classification as an enrichment plugin in the ingest Kafka consumer, add sensitivity field to audit schema (v2), update indexer to create sensitivity-aware partitions, and add retention engine hooks for cold-store archiving.
tradeoffs: Extra CPU at ingest for classification increases cost; mitigated by making rules deterministic and small (regex + event type lookup).
Tenant-aware partitioning increases shard count but reduces reindex/purge scope — requires shard autoscaler adjustments.
WORM cold snapshots add complexity for legal/forensics exports but ensure compliance; cost tradeoff vs. keeping everything in hot index.
Sampling low-sensitivity events may impact analytics fidelity for customers; full raw can be offered as an opt-in paid feature.
Query-time summaries speed investigations but require periodic jobs to keep them fresh; storage/resource tradeoff vs. on-the-fly aggregation.
acceptance_criteria: Ingest adds "sensitivity" tag for all SSO/SAML and admin events per ruleset and documented mapping.
High-sensitivity events are retained in hot index for a minimum of 90 days and archived to cold WORM object store for 1 year by default.
Per-tenant storage estimator surface appears in Console and raises alert when 90% of guardrail is reached.
End-to-end benchmark: no more than 5ms median additional latency for the ingest enrichment step at 95th percentile load (baseline: current ingest pipeline).
Sampling/backpressure policy triggers correctly under simulated tenant overload and only affects low-sensitivity events while preserving high-sensitivity writes.
E2E test scenario: SOC runbook for role-escalation incident uses fast audit lookup to find the three most recent admin role changes for a tenant in <2s.
Security review completed and signed off by Security and Compliance owners.
notes: Initial rule set drafted with PM/Security — attached to Confluence (link below).
Prototype ingest plugin validated on staging with 10k EPS, classification CPU overhead ~3%.
Discussed cold-store encryption & KMS integration with infra; must support tenant-scoped key access controls for Private deployments.
Decision: use existing Kafka topic + enrichment consumer rather than adding a second stream to reduce end-to-end complexity.
Follow-ups: UI controls for rule editing to be a separate PM ticket; cross-team sync with billing for guardrail enforcement.
